item.title: No. 5 have fenced off and laid decorative stone over part of the public footpath, creating private access and obstructing public manhole covers. A new ad hoc side gate has also been inserted into the wall between Nos. 5 and 6, altering the original boundary line. Historic Google images show this area was previously open (and now) adopted highway; as does the FixMyStreet Map., 19th July
item.description:
Location: Directly outside 5 Stearman Walk, on the shared public footpath between Nos. 5 and 6. Within the past week, the occupants of No. 5 have fenced off and surfaced part of the public footpath with decorative stone, creating a private side path leading to a newly installed ad hoc side gate. This now blocks access to public manhole covers and turns part of the adopted footpath into private space. Concerns: – A section of public footpath has been enclosed and is being used as private access (especially with regards to the ad hoc side gate). – Access to public manhole covers is obstructed. – The original boundary wall has been cut into to create a new gateway that did not previously exist. – These changes appear to have been carried out without planning permission and alter the approved layout of the development. Requested action: – Please investigate and confirm the highway boundary. – If this area is adopted public footpath, I request that the council: • Require removal of the fence, decorative stone, and gate. • Ensure the footpath and access to manhole covers are reinstated. • Notify utility companies if their access is blocked. • Consider whether planning enforcement is needed for the alteration of the building frontage (in respect of the new gate).

Nearest road to the pin placed on the map (automatically generated by OpenStreetMap): Lobleys Drive, Hucclecote, Tewkesbury
Report on FixMyStreet
